summary: The change makes TypeCollector tolerate invalid key contracts: it guards the intMembers/stringMembers Add calls with ContainsKey and, in the property loop only, skips a member after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys; it also adds README text, analyzer tests and execution tests. The contract diagnostics for SuppressSourceGeneration types (F1) and the suppression of generation-only diagnostics (F2) were already produced on base (their tests pass in the source-reverted run), so the real fix is the crash hardening (N1), and that is incomplete: the field loop got a blank line where the property loop got `continue;`, so a mixed-key-kind field still dereferences a null key and crashes the analyzer. Not ready to merge until the field path matches the property path and has a test.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: The F1 tests pass at head, but they also passed with the source reverted, so the requirement was already met on base and this change adds no F1 behaviour. Duplicate and mixed keys are reported for property members (the *WithoutAnalyzerFailure tests pass at head).
The suppressed type returns from GetObjectInfo before the partial-type check, and the F2 test passes at head. It also passed on base, so this was already met before the change.

The property loop now skips a mixed-kind member (line 1008), but the field loop still falls through after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys (line 1147, blank line 1148). A field whose key kind differs from the first key reaches `intKey!.Value` on a null int key (line 1154) or `stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!)` with a null string key (line 1170), and either one throws inside the analyzer. The full suite passes only because no test has mixed-kind fields.

evidence.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: 4 of the 8 new analyzer tests fail with the source reverted (each fails on the AD0001 crash), and the full suite passes at head (175/175) with no regressions. The field-loop path in N1 is not covered by any test.

findings.title: Field loop still crashes on mixed int/string keys (missing continue)
findings.claim: In the field loop, the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys branch now ends in a blank line (1148) instead of the `continue;` added to the property loop at 1008, so execution falls through. If the first key is an int and a later field has a string key, `isIntKey` is true and `intKey` is null, so `intKey!.Value` at 1154 throws InvalidOperationException. In the reverse case, the else branch at 1168 has no `stringKey is not null` guard, so `stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!)` at 1170 throws ArgumentNullException. `searchFirst`/`isIntKey` carry over from the property loop, so an int-keyed property followed by a string-keyed field also crashes. The result is an AD0001 analyzer crash or a generator failure on an invalid contract, which REQ-2234-N1 forbids, and this library's analyzer runs on user code.

evidence.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members

findings.suggested_fix: Replace the blank line at 1148 with `continue;`, matching line 1008. Add analyzer tests with mixed key kinds on fields (int then string, string then int, and an int-keyed property followed by a string-keyed field).

findings.title: Crash tests cover only properties; the field path is untested
findings.claim: Every new *WithoutAnalyzerFailure test declares its members as properties (e.g. `public string Member2 { get; set; }`), so the separate field loop (lines 1124-1192), which has its own duplicate and mixed-key handling, is never exercised. That is how the defect in N1 gets through a full suite that passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add field-based duplicate-key and mixed-key tests for both suppressed and generated types.

findings.title: F1/F2 tests already pass on base; the change only fixes the crash
findings.claim: The three F1 tests and the F2 test pass with the source reverted, so they do not demonstrate this change. The only behaviour the change adds is not crashing on duplicate or mixed keys, which the commit message ('The analyzer does not work') and the README section do not make clear.
